name: Mallinatha
role: 19th Tirthankara of the present Jain age
summary: Jain texts say the 19th Tirthankara, Mallinatha, was born in Mithila, with a water pitcher as emblem. Shvetambaras remember Malli as a woman who taught six kings with a golden statue; Digambaras remember a prince.
about: In Jain tradition Mallinatha is the 19th of the 24 ford-makers (tirthankaras) of the present descending age. Jain texts say Mallinatha was born at Mithila to King Kumbha and Queen Prabhavati (called Prajnavati in some lists) of the Ikshvaku line, and became a siddha, a liberated soul, on Mount Shikharji. The two main Jain sects tell the story differently. Shvetambara texts say Malli was a woman and use this to teach that women can reach liberation. Digambara texts say Mallinatha was a prince. Both traditions honour Mallinatha with temples across India, and the idol is known by a water pitcher (kalasha) carved below it. In the Svetambara account, Malli taught six suitor kings about the body through a hollow golden statue.
kidSummary: Mallinatha is one of the 24 Tirthankaras, wise teachers in Jainism who show others the way to be free. Mallinatha was born in the city of Mithila, and the symbol is a water pitcher. Some Jains remember Mallinatha as a princess called Malli, and others as a prince. Both groups love and honour Malli.

story.title: A royal birth in Mithila
story.text: Jain stories say a baby was born in the city of Mithila to King Kumbha and Queen Prabhavati, also called Prajnavati. This child would grow up to be a Tirthankara.

story.title: Two ways to remember Malli
story.text: Shvetambara Jains remember the child as a princess called Mallivati. Digambara Jains remember a prince. Both groups still honour Mallinatha.

story.title: The golden statue
story.text: Svetambara texts say six kings wanted to marry Malli. In Hemachandra's version she had a hollow golden statue made and put a little food inside it every day. When she lifted its lid, the smell taught the kings that the body does not last.

story.title: Letting go
story.text: When grown, Mallinatha gave up palace life to follow the path of a monk. Jain tradition says the soul had been preparing for this over many lifetimes.

story.title: Light and teaching
story.text: After deep meditation Mallinatha is said to have gained perfect knowledge, and then taught others to be gentle and to let go of greed.

story.title: Freedom on the mountain
story.text: Jains believe Mallinatha was freed from birth and rebirth at Shikharji, a mountain that many pilgrims still climb.

teaches: Letting go of greed and attachment
Everyone can walk the path to freedom

facts.text: The name Malli means jasmine: Jainpedia says her mother craved jasmine flowers during pregnancy, and the baby was named for them.
Shvetambara Jains hold that Mallinatha was a woman named Malli or Mallivati. Digambara Jains hold that every tirthankara was male. This is one of the biggest differences between the two sects.

Svetambara texts say that in an earlier life as a king, Mallinatha secretly outdid friends in fasting. They name that deceit as the cause of a female birth. Digambara accounts describe a blameless ascetic instead.
In 1982 children playing in Asigarh Fort at Hansi, Haryana, found 58 buried Jain bronzes, Mallinatha among them. Devotees seem to have hidden them around 1037 CE as a raid approached.
The 1586 Chaturmukha Basadi in Karkala has life-size Mallinatha idols facing the four cardinal directions, standing with Aranatha and Munisuvrata.
In Hemachandra's Svetambara account, Malli had a golden statue of herself made, hollow inside, and each day dropped a ball of food into it, then covered the opening with a golden lotus.
Six kings, friends of Malli from an earlier birth, wanted to marry her; when her father refused they besieged Mithila, says Jainpedia.
When Malli lifted the lotus lid of the statue, the awful smell shocked the kings, and she used the moment to teach that the body is not worth clinging to.

Jainpedia says Malli was initiated and became all-knowing on the same day, skipping the usual years of wandering. Birth, initiation and omniscience each fall on an 11th lunar day, marked as Maunaikadashi.
On Mount Girnar, a Mallinatha temple built in 1230 is among the first shrines pilgrims reach on the climb, says Jainpedia.

quiz.q: Which object is the emblem of Mallinatha?
quiz.why: The water pitcher (kalasha) is the sign that lets worshippers recognise Mallinatha.

quiz.q: In which city do Jain texts say Mallinatha was born?
quiz.why: Mithila is named as the birthplace in Jain texts.

quiz.q: What is the biggest disagreement between the two big Jain sects about Mallinatha?
options: The colour of the water pitcher
Whether Mallinatha was a woman or a man
quiz.why: Shvetambaras say Malli was a woman; Digambaras say a man.

quiz.q: What does the name Malli mean, according to Jainpedia?
quiz.why: Her mother craved jasmine flowers during pregnancy, and the baby was named for them.

quiz.q: In the Svetambara story, what did Malli hide inside a hollow golden statue to teach six kings?
quiz.why: The food rotted and the smell taught the kings that the body decays.
